title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a (metrisable) stratified space with strata indexed by a poset I. X_i^* is the open, locally closed stratum and X_i its closure, with ∂X_{i0} = ∪_{i<i0} X_i^*. V_i = V(X_i^*, X) is a 'prévoisinage tubulaire' (tubular pre-neighbourhood) of the stratum X_i^*. For a flag i0<...<in, V_{i0...in} = V_{i0}∩...∩V_{in}. This is the device of Esquisse d'un programme §5: describe the stratified homotopy type by the diagram of spaces V_d indexed by flags d.

Step 1, restriction to a subspace. For a subset Z ⊂ X, set V^Z_{i0...in} = V_{i0...in} ∩ Z (99). An abandoned hypothesis is crossed out: that Z contain a difference X_{in} − X_{i0}. The retained version is that Z is locally closed and contains the top stratum X_{in}^* of the flag. The claim (100) is that the inclusion V^Z_{i0...in} → V_{i0...in} is a homotopy equivalence. Grothendieck marks it '? à vérifier!' and adds 'on suppose X métrisable'. The heuristic is that a flag tube V_{i0...in} retracts onto its trace on the top stratum X_{in}^*, which is the generalised homotopy link of the flag. So any Z containing that trace should see the same homotopy type.

Step 2, from indices to bands. Indices are generalised to 'bandes' J ⊂ I (presumably convex subposets, so that X_J^* = ∪_{j∈J} X_j^* is locally closed), and flags of indices to flags of bands J0 ≤ ... ≤ Jn. Definition (101): V_J = V(X_J^*, X), the tubular pre-neighbourhood of the union of strata in J. It is computed in two ways:
- V_J = ∪_{j∈J} V_j;
- V_J = colim_{d ∈ Drap(J)} V_d, the colimit over the poset of flags in J.
The note says these formulas hold for an arbitrary subset J. This is a Čech/nerve-type gluing formula: the union of the tubes of the strata is the colimit of the flag-indexed intersections.

Step 3, consequences. Set V^Z_J = V_J ∩ Z (102). Then:
- (103) X_J^* → V_J is a homotopy equivalence (tubular neighbourhood axiom).
- (104) If Z ⊇ X_J^* (written X_J on the page, evidently X_J^*), then X_J^* → V^Z_J → V_J are homotopy equivalences, and V^Z_J = V(X_J^*, Z).
The last point is a compatibility of the tube construction with restriction to subspaces.

Next page. The colimit formula is restricted to Z (105). Mixed tubes V_{J,L} = V_J ∩ V_L are introduced (106). For J ≤ L, V_{J,L} is expressed as a colimit over the flags in J∪L that meet both J and L, i.e. flags starting in J and ending in L (107–108).

Purpose. This is preparation for the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space: replacing it by a diagram of tubes and links indexed by flags of bands. The constructions must be stable under passing to sub-unions of strata and under restriction to subspaces Z, so that the unfolding can be done inductively.
errors: (100) is explicitly flagged by Grothendieck as unverified. As stated, for an arbitrary locally closed Z ⊇ X_{in}^*, it seems to need more than metrisability. The retraction of V_{i0...in} onto its trace on X_{in}^* must be compatible with Z, or Z must be a union of strata or otherwise 'tame'. Otherwise Z can add pieces in lower strata that change the homotopy type. The hypothesis was being adjusted on the page (crossed-out alternatives).
(104) writes the hypothesis as Z ⊃ X_J. Given the arrow X_J^* → V_J^Z and the identification V_J^Z = V(X_J^*, Z), the intended hypothesis is presumably Z ⊃ X_J^* (as in (105) on the next page).
The identification V_J^Z = V(X_J^*, Z) presupposes that the pre-tubular neighbourhood construction V(−,−) is intrinsic and commutes with restriction to subspaces. This is not justified on the page.

The equality ∪_{j∈J} V_j = colim_{Drap(J)} V_d is fine as a set-theoretic/open-cover colimit. As a homotopy colimit it requires the V_d to form an open cover with good intersection behaviour, which is implicit.

ideas.what: Diagram of tubular neighbourhood intersections V_{i0...in} indexed by flags of strata, encoding the stratified homotopy type
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / exit-path ∞-category data; diagram of generalised homotopy links indexed by the subdivision sd(I)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Lurie HA App. A; Douteau–Waas; Haine; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (outline of tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods); details only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: Tubes of unions of strata over a band: V_J = ∪_{j∈J} V_j = colim over flags in J of V_d
ideas.modern_name: Čech/nerve colimit decomposition of a regular neighbourhood of a union of strata; homotopy links for subposets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Mather control data; for general subposets in Douteau's generalised homotopy links

ideas.what: Restriction of tubes to a subspace Z containing the relevant strata preserves homotopy type (V^Z → V homotopy equivalence; V_J^Z = V(X_J^*, Z))
ideas.modern_name: Locality/restriction invariance of homotopy links; stratified homotopy invariance of neighbourhood germs

ideas.what: Flags of bands J0 ≤ ... ≤ Jn as indexing objects (coarsening of the stratification poset)
ideas.modern_name: Coarsening of stratifications along convex subposets / interval decompositions; stratified spaces over subdivided posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Haine, Douteau, Nand-Lal (stratified homotopy theory over posets)

missed.claim: Grothendieck left open, and flagged, the precise hypotheses under which intersecting a flag tube V_{i0...in} with a locally closed Z ⊇ X_{in}^* is a homotopy equivalence. This is a restriction-invariance lemma for generalised homotopy links in metrisable stratified spaces.
missed.quote: si Z est une partie loc^t fermée contenant X_{in}^* ... alors on a V^Z_{i0...in} ↪ V_{i0...in} (équiv. d'homotopie) ... ? à vérifier!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern stratified homotopy theory (Douteau–Waas, Haine) works with homotopy links via path spaces rather than actual neighbourhoods. A clean neighbourhood-level restriction lemma would connect Grothendieck's 'déploiement' with these. It is likely known in special cases (e.g. for Quinn's or Hughes' teardrop neighbourhoods) rather than genuinely new.

missed.claim: A systematic calculus of tubes indexed by flags of 'bands' (convex subposets) is set up: V_J, V_{J0...Jn}, and mixed tubes V_{J,L} written as colimits over flags starting in J and ending in L. This anticipates the functoriality of homotopy links under coarsening of the stratifying poset.
missed.quote: On va généraliser la définition des V_i, V_{i0...in} en des V_J, V_{J0...Jn}, où J est une des bandes de I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Coarsening/refinement functoriality is an active technical topic in poset-stratified homotopy theory. This is an early, unpublished version of that bookkeeping, but more of historical than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is technical bookkeeping for the unpublished 'déploiement' programme sketched in Esquisse §5. The ideas (flag-indexed tube diagrams, homotopy links, coarsening by bands) are now standard in Quinn/Lurie/AFT/Douteau–Haine form. The restriction lemma (100) is self-flagged as unverified and is plausible but not striking.
transcription_corrections: 'où J est une partie [?] des bornée [?] de I' should read roughly 'où J est une des bandes de I, resp. J0 < ... < Jn est un drapeau de bandes'. The word is 'bande(s)', not 'bornée'.
'"drapeau de bornées" des I' → 'drapeau de bandes' de I.
Crossed-out line: 'NB Ẋ_{i0} = X_{i0} ∩ X^*_{i0} = ∪_{i<i0} X_{in}' — the middle term looks like X_{i0} − X^*_{i0} (boundary of the closed stratum), and the unions are ∪_{i<i0} X_i = ∪_{i<i0} X_i^*.
In (104) the first arrow X_J^* → V_J^Z also carries the homotopy-equivalence mark (h~), and V(X_J^*, Z) is written under V_J^Z as an identification.
Insertion after 'loc^t fermée' reads 'contenant X_{in}^*' with a parenthetical about V^Z_{in} ↪ V_{in}; the transcribed '(de sorte que X_{in} ∩ V^Z_{in} ↪ V_{in})' is uncertain.
'(on suppose X métrisable...)' is plausible; the page reads approximately 'on suppose X métrisable...'.
